newsitem.title: USA: Lilco seeks to extend rate freeze.
newsitem.headline: Lilco seeks to extend rate freeze.

text.p: Long Island Lighting Co said Friday it will ask the state Public Service Commission to continue the freeze on its base electric rates through the end of the century.
The request will come in the utility's three year filing with the commission, which postponed a decision on Lilco's temporary rates early this month by removing the case from its September 11 agenda.
In July, the commission ordered an expedited proceeding to consider temporary rates for Lilco.
When the decision was postponed, commission spokesman Dave Flanagan said the next possible time for the commission to take the case would be at its October 2 meeting.
However, the case is not on the agenda for Wednesday's meeting, a spokeswoman said Friday.
Lilco officials were not immediately available to comment on whether the utility's planned filing was in response to the proceeding the commission initiated in July.
"Electric rates have been frozen since 1994 and, under this proposal, the freeze will remain in place through the end of 1999, a six-year period," the company's statement said.

It said the filing also assumes a one-year reduction in rates of of 1.1 percent in 1997 as a result of increased sales due to the hot summer of 1995, but assumes no other rate reductions. -- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710
